name: Pusher Beams
description: Pusher Beams is a hosted push-notification service for iOS, Android, and web applications. It manages device push tokens and supports anonymous Device Interests, authenticated users, delivery insights, webhooks, and realtime debugging.
agentUseSummary: Add one Beams instance ID and secret key, then bind one anonymous Device Interest; agents can send a single bounded title/body notification to that interest under Relay approval policy.

credentialRequirements.name: PUSHER_BEAMS_INSTANCE_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Pusher Beams instance ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter the exact UUID instance ID. Relay uses it in both the allowlisted HTTPS host and path.

credentialRequirements.name: PUSHER_BEAMS_SECRET_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Pusher Beams secret key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use the instance secret key from Credentials. Relay encrypts it and sends it only as a Bearer header to the exact instance host.

credentialRequirements.name: PUSHER_BEAMS_INTEREST
credentialRequirements.label: Bound Device Interest
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter one anonymous Device Interest. Relay permits notifications only to this exact interest.

capabilities.label: Publish to one Device Interest
capabilities.description: Send one title/body notification to the exact connection-bound anonymous interest across configured APNs, FCM, and web platforms.

approvalRequired.label: Publish Pusher Beams interest notification
approvalRequired.description: Send one bounded title/body notification to the single connection-bound Device Interest.

blocked.label: Access users, devices, or tokens
blocked.description: Authenticated user IDs, device IDs/tokens, platform tokens, Beams auth tokens, subscriptions, and per-device state remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary interests or payloads
blocked.description: Runtime interests, multiple interests, user targeting, webhook URLs, custom data, deep links, media, platform overrides, and raw payloads remain blocked.

blocked.label: Delete, configure, or administer Beams
blocked.description: User/device deletion, interest changes, credentials, instances, platform configuration, webhooks, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: Arbitrary instances, origins, paths, methods, headers, bodies, SDK surfaces, retries, browser sessions, bulk targeting, and exports remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Every external notification requires approval; users, devices, arbitrary targets/payloads, administration, raw APIs, and bulk remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same one-interest notification runs directly; exact binding, content/size caps, provider limits, audits, and provider authorization remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one exact-interest Pusher Beams notification wrapper with approval and payload bounds.
Hermes receives the same exact-interest Pusher Beams notification wrapper with approval and payload bounds.

providerSetup.blocker: Pusher Beams publishing requires an eligible instance, configured push platforms, an instance secret key, and an existing anonymous Device Interest.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer admin supplies the exact instance credentials and interest, confirms its subscribed audience, and completes one approval-controlled live notification acceptance test.

evidence.supports: Pusher documents Bearer secret-key authentication, the exact instance host/path, one-to-100 Device Interests, a 10 KiB request limit, publishId response, 100 RPS limit, and provider errors.
Pusher documents instance ID/secret-key server credentials and APNs, FCM, and web title/body publishing through Device Interests.
Pusher documents Device Interests as anonymous device groups and restricts names to 164 allowlisted ASCII characters.
Pusher documents Beams as a hosted multi-platform push service with users, interests, token management, insights, webhooks, and debugging; Relay mounts only exact-interest publishing.

securityNotes: The instance ID, secret key, and interest are encrypted references; the secret is sent only as a Bearer header to the UUID-derived pushnotifications.pusher.com host.

Relay fixes POST /publish_api/v1/instances/{same-instance}/publishes/interests, one bound interest, three title/body-only platform payloads, no webhook, redirects denied, 30 seconds, 10 KiB request, and 1 MB response.
Title is capped at 100 characters and body at 1000; arbitrary interests, users, custom data, links, media, platform overrides, tokens, SDK surfaces, retries, and bulk remain blocked.

Safe mode requires approval bound to the connection and action; Dangerous mode removes only Relay per-action approval, not provider authority, target binding, caps, audits, or truthful error handling.
Provider setup, secret capture, audience verification, and live acceptance remain customer/external steps.
